group.title: Describing words
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: Correct in every detail, with no mistakes.
examples: The weather report was {accurate}: it rained at noon.
wrong: The clock is accurate, so it is always an hour wrong.

words.meaning: Real, not just imagined or expected.
examples: The {actual} cost was much higher than we planned.
wrong: The actual price was only a guess that nobody checked.

words.meaning: Normal or usual, not very good or very bad.
examples: It was an {average} day, nothing special.
wrong: She is an average singer, the best the world has ever heard.

words.meaning: Simple and needed first, before harder things.
examples: You only need {basic} math to do this job.
wrong: The course is basic, so only experts can follow it.

words.meaning: Lasting only a short time or using few words.
examples: She gave a {brief} answer and sat down.
wrong: His speech was brief: it went on for three hours.

words.meaning: Having many parts and hard to understand.
examples: The instructions were so {complicated} that I gave up.
wrong: The game is complicated, so a small child learned it in a minute.

words.meaning: Very, very big.
examples: An {enormous} ship sailed into the port.
wrong: The enormous mouse fit easily in my hand.

words.meaning: Whole, with every part included.
examples: We spent the {entire} weekend at the beach.
wrong: I read the entire book, except for most of the chapters.

words.meaning: Very important and really needed.
examples: Water is {essential} for all living things.
wrong: A warm coat is essential, so you don’t need to bring one.

words.meaning: Very great, far beyond what is usual.
examples: The desert has {extreme} heat in summer.
wrong: The cold was extreme, so we didn’t even need a jacket.

words.meaning: Not interesting or exciting in any way.
examples: The lecture was so {dull} that I nearly fell asleep.
wrong: The film was dull, so we sat on the edge of our seats the whole time.

words.meaning: Known to you because you have seen or heard it before.
examples: Her face looks {familiar}; have we met?
wrong: The song was familiar, so I had never heard it before.

words.meaning: The best possible for a certain purpose.
examples: This quiet room is {ideal} for studying.
wrong: The ideal hotel was dirty, noisy and far away.

words.meaning: Making you feel admiration because it is so good or big.
examples: Her painting was really {impressive}.
wrong: The show was impressive, so everyone left bored halfway.

words.meaning: So good, big or surprising that it is hard to believe.
examples: The view from the mountain was {incredible}.
wrong: It was an incredible match where nothing exciting happened.

words.meaning: Easy to see or understand.
examples: It was {obvious} that she was tired.
wrong: The answer was obvious, so nobody could ever find it.

words.meaning: Normal and not special in any way.
examples: It was just an {ordinary} Tuesday.
wrong: It was an ordinary day: aliens landed in the park.

words.meaning: New and different, not copied from something else.
examples: She had an {original} idea for the party.
wrong: His story was original because he copied it from a book.

words.meaning: Single and special, not any other.
examples: Is there a {particular} film you want to see?
wrong: I want this particular shirt, but any shirt will do.

words.meaning: Nice and enjoyable.
examples: We had a {pleasant} walk by the river.
wrong: The evening was pleasant, and everyone was miserable.

words.meaning: Useful and sensible for real life.
examples: Comfortable shoes are more {practical} for walking.
wrong: High heels are the most practical shoes for a long hike.

words.meaning: Coming before the one now or the one you mean.
examples: I met him the {previous} week.
wrong: The previous owner will move into the house next year.

words.meaning: Not happening or seen very often.
examples: Snow is {rare} in this hot city.
wrong: This bird is rare, so you see thousands every day.

words.meaning: Happening or made a short time ago.
examples: Have you seen her {recent} photos?
wrong: In recent news from a hundred years ago, the king died.

words.meaning: Happening again and again at the same times.
examples: Take {regular} breaks when you study.
wrong: He is a regular visitor; he came once ten years ago.

words.meaning: Almost the same as something else.
examples: Our jackets are {similar}, but mine is darker.
wrong: The twins look similar: one is tall and blond, the other short and dark.

words.meaning: Clear and exact, about one thing only.
examples: Can you give me a {specific} example?
wrong: Give me a specific time, like ’sometime next year’.

words.meaning: Right for a certain person, purpose or situation.
examples: This film isn’t {suitable} for young children.
wrong: Flip-flops are suitable shoes for climbing a snowy mountain.

words.meaning: Having the usual qualities of a certain kind of thing.
examples: Rice is a {typical} food in this region.
wrong: It was a typical summer day, with snow falling all morning.

words.meaning: Different from what normally happens; not common.
examples: It’s {unusual} for him to be late.
wrong: It is unusual to see cars on a busy city road.

words.meaning: Worth a lot of money, or very useful.
examples: Keep your {valuable} things in the hotel safe.
wrong: The ring is valuable, so it cost almost nothing.

words.meaning: Several different kinds of.
examples: The shop sells {various} kinds of tea.
wrong: The café offers various drinks: only water.

words.meaning: Very bad or unpleasant.
examples: The food was {awful}, so we left early.
wrong: The movie was awful, so we want to see it again and again.

words.meaning: Very good, clever or bright.
examples: What a {brilliant} idea!
wrong: His brilliant plan failed because it made no sense at all.

words.meaning: From a time very long ago.
examples: We visited an {ancient} temple from 500 BC.
wrong: The ancient building was finished last month.

words.meaning: Small from one side to the other.
examples: The street is too {narrow} for a bus.
wrong: The road was narrow, so four trucks drove side by side.

words.meaning: Flat and even, with no rough parts.
examples: The baby’s skin is so {smooth}.
wrong: The road was smooth and full of holes and bumps.

words.meaning: Easy, useful or fitting well with your plans.
examples: The shop is in a {convenient} place near my home.
wrong: The time was convenient, so I couldn’t come at all.

words.meaning: Lasting only for a short time.
examples: She has a {temporary} job for the summer.
wrong: This is a temporary home; we will live here forever.

words.meaning: Lasting for a very long time or forever.
examples: After a year, he got a {permanent} job.
wrong: The ink is permanent, so it washes off with water.
